primaryCurrencyNotes.BHS: The Bahamian dollar is pegged 1:1 to, and co-circulates with, the US dollar.
primaryCurrencyNotes.BRN: The Brunei dollar is Brunei's own currency. The Brunei-Singapore Currency Interchangeability Agreement (1967) makes SGD interchangeable and also legal tender, but BND is Brunei's own.
primaryCurrencyNotes.BTN: The ngultrum is Bhutan's own currency (its ISO 4217 code happens to be the same three letters as Bhutan's cca3, BTN), pegged 1:1 to and co-circulating with the Indian rupee.
primaryCurrencyNotes.CUB: Cuba abolished the convertible peso (CUC) on 1 January 2021, unifying to the Cuban peso (CUP); mledoze's snapshot still lists both for CUB. CUP is chosen as primary; CUC is kept in the output, marked questionable/obsolete (see QUESTIONABLE_CODES), not dropped.
primaryCurrencyNotes.KHM: The riel is Cambodia's own, central-bank-issued currency; the US dollar circulates widely alongside it, but KHR remains the official legal tender.
primaryCurrencyNotes.KIR: Same arrangement as Tuvalu: the Kiribati dollar (KID) is coins only, pegged 1:1 to and co-circulating with AUD.
primaryCurrencyNotes.LSO: Same arrangement as Eswatini and Namibia: the loti is pegged 1:1 to and co-circulates with the South African rand.
primaryCurrencyNotes.NAM: Same arrangement as Eswatini: the Namibian dollar is pegged 1:1 to and co-circulates with the South African rand.
primaryCurrencyNotes.PAN: The balboa is Panama's own currency by name and the one normally given as the answer, but Panama mints only balboa coins and uses US dollar banknotes for paper money, so USD is the currency actually seen day to day -- flagged as uncertain.
primaryCurrencyNotes.PSE: No official currency; usage differs by area (ILS and JOD mainly in the West Bank, EGP mainly in Gaza) and mledoze's data gives no signal either way. Reported, not guessed: primaryCurrency is null for PSE.
primaryCurrencyNotes.SWZ: The lilangeni is Eswatini's own currency, pegged 1:1 to and co-circulating with the South African rand.
primaryCurrencyNotes.TUV: Tuvalu issues no banknotes; the Tuvaluan dollar (TVD) exists only as coins pegged 1:1 to, and used alongside, the Australian dollar, which is the currency actually used in everyday transactions.
primaryCurrencyNotes.ZWE: Of the multi-currency basket mledoze lists (legalised 2009-2019 and still widely used in practice), the US dollar has been the dominant transaction currency for most of that period; no Zimbabwean-dollar code (ZWL/ZWG) appears in this mledoze snapshot to prefer instead. Low confidence -- flagged.
